rows.subtype: Approach: rehearses a speech in the mind and in front of a mirror [Action]
rows.description: A girl preparing a class talk imagines the room, practises the opening line in front of the mirror, and notices where she forgets the second point.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.subtype: Approach: imagines the route and timings of an event day [Thinking]
rows.description: A student walking through the interview day in his head, from bus to waiting room, realises he had not planned where to keep his file dry in the monsoon.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 18–22, 23–26

rows.subtype: Approach: imagines only the successful path and ignores obstacles [Pitfall]
rows.description: A student pictures a perfect presentation, applause and all, and never rehearses what to do if the projector fails. The simulation made him feel ready without preparing him.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 23–26

rows.subtype: Approach: simulates both success and things going wrong and prepares a response [Revision]
rows.description: A presenter adds a run-through of a dead laptop and a tough question, and carries a printed copy of the slides and a short prepared answer.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22

rows.subtype: Approach: asks what if for the main risks and writes a plan B [Thinking]
rows.description: A teenager organising a cricket match asks what if it rains and arranges an indoor game or a reserved date with the school, so the day is not lost.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 18–22, 23–26

rows.subtype: Approach: prepares a backup for the likely thing that could go wrong [Action]
rows.description: A student travelling for an exam by train books a bus option as well, and notes the timings, in case the train is delayed by fog.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 23–26

rows.subtype: Approach: sets triggers for switching to plan B [Action]
rows.description: An event organiser decides that if fewer than sixty confirmations arrive by Friday, then she will move to the smaller hall, rather than deciding under pressure on the day.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 18–22

rows.subtype: Approach: plans for so many scenarios that the main plan is neglected [Pitfall]
rows.description: A project lead writes backup plans for twelve risks, many of them unlikely, and runs out of time to prepare the main path, which then falters.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 18–22

rows.subtype: Approach: prunes the list to the few likely, costly risks and revisits after each phase [Revision]
rows.description: The lead keeps three contingencies with clear triggers and reviews them at each milestone, dropping any that no longer apply.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 18–22

rows.subtype: Approach: leaves extra time before something starts [Action]
rows.description: A boy who takes twenty minutes to reach the bus stop leaves at thirty because last week a friend stopped him to talk and he nearly missed the bus.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 18–22, 23–26
